Canonical ids of source records

Source: R/targets.R
soil_resolve_targets.Rd

Finds the canonical ids (target_id, and the feature_id, profile_id, component_id, horizon_id it belongs to) of records known by their source identity: provider, dataset, release, level and the source record id (POST /query/targets/resolve). It is the step before publishing derived values (soil_publish_values()) on records known by their source ids. Targets are sent in requests of at most 10,000.

Usage

soil_resolve_targets(soil = soil_session(), targets, strict = TRUE)

Arguments

soil

A session; the default session when omitted. Client-side: not sent to the API.

targets

A data frame with the columns provider_code, dataset_code (lower-case codes), release_code, target_level ("feature", "profile", "component", "horizon"), source_record_id and optionally source_table, without NA (except in source_table). API field targets.

strict

Stop with soilhub_argument_error (argument targets) when a target is missing or ambiguous; the full resolution is in the error's resolution field. Client-side: not sent to the API.

Value

A data frame, one row per row of targets and in the same order: input_index (0-based position in targets), status, provider_code, dataset_code, release_code, target_level, source_record_id, source_table, release_status, target_id, feature_id, profile_id, component_id, horizon_id, source_support, geometry_kind, top_depth_cm, bottom_depth_cm, candidate_count (integer). Attribute soil_metadata: the request ids and status_counts.

Details

Each target is resolved (one canonical record), missing (none) or ambiguous (several: give source_table to choose). With strict = TRUE (the default) any missing or ambiguous target is an error, so a later publication never uses a partial resolution; with strict = FALSE the statuses are returned for inspection.

Rights: soil:read. Capability: target_resolution.

See also

Other thematic reads: soil_health_scores(), soil_health_summary(), soil_ttr_flags(), soil_values(), soil_values_summary()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
keys <- data.frame(provider_code = "isric", dataset_code = "wosis_points",
                   release_code = "2023-12", target_level = "profile",
                   source_record_id = c("101", "102"))
ids <- soil_resolve_targets(soil, keys)
ids$target_id

# inspect instead of stopping
res <- soil_resolve_targets(soil, keys, strict = FALSE)
table(res$status)
} # }
